thread:
maria: Incoming ask from CX Bank: long-term archival evidence they can independently verify. They mentioned 'signed archives' + ability to validate chain-of-custody.
ben: Do we have a shaped proposal? We currently offer retention tiers but not verifiable signed snapshots tied to customer KMS.
sarah: Clarify with customer: do they need WORM storage semantics or is a signed manifest sufficient for auditors? That affects both legal language and implementation.
kevin: Implementation note: cheap path = daily NDJSON snapshots stored in cold blob with a signed manifest. Search over 10y is $$$.
olivia: Legal: auditors typically accept signed exports + attestations, but the contract must call out rotation windows, key escrow (if any), and non-repudiation guarantees.
evidence-bot: export-service: snapshot job queued (id=exp-2026-04-01-42)
maria: Product idea: a new "archival evidence" add-on. Features: signed NDJSON + manifest, export checksum preview, optional PII redaction, export notarization metadata, and evidence TTL 7-10y+.
ben: Config prototype for discussion:
```
archive_profile: {
  name: "evidentiary-10y",
  retention: "10y",
  indexable: false,
  signed_manifest: true,
  signer: "customer-kms|redwood-hsm",
  pre_sign_preview: true,
  redaction_modes: ["pii-mask","token-strip"]
}
```
sarah: UX question: do we need an admin-only export console + audit trail or allow API-triggered exports? Probably both.
kevin: Ops: Export generation time depends on dataset size. For SLA: propose 24h for large archives, 4h for <50GB. We'll quantify. Also need a streaming sign step to avoid costly rehydrate.
maria: Pricing thought: charge per-GB archived + per-signature operation + optional KMS attestation fee. Sales wants a per-customer proposal for CX Bank.
olivia: Also require CI for verification tooling so customers can run local verification against signed manifests. Need docs and a simple CLI.
evidence-bot: export-service: exp-2026-04-01-42 status -> archived:pending-signature
ben: Security: if they bring their own KMS (BYOK), acceptance criteria must include proof of key ownership, rotation policy (retention-safe rotations), and a documented escrow/lockbox path if keys are revoked.
sarah: Product acceptance criteria (first draft): 1) Export manifest includes checksums, schema version, signing key id, timestamp; 2) Redaction options applied before signature; 3) Verification CLI and reproducible checksum flow; 4) SLAs for export generation (small/medium/large); 5) Legal attestation template for customers.
kevin: Engineering tasks: storage lifecycle (hot->cold->coldest), sign-on-write vs sign-on-export options, cost estimates for egress + CPU for signing at scale. I'll run numbers and push to the epic.
maria: Also surface to compliance: does SOC2/ISO need special metadata (e.g., signer chain, HSM attestation) for 'immutable evidence'?
olivia: I'll check with our external assessor and draft contract wording.
ben: UX: include an "Export preview" step showing record count + sample checksum and require explicit acceptance before final sign. That helps disputes.
sarah: I'll drop a PRD stub into the compliance epic with that AC list and a proposed timeline (MVP in Q3, GA in Q4 if blocked by legal).
maria: Action items recap: - Sarah: PRD stub + ACs - Kevin: cost model + engineering estimate - Ben: verification CLI spec + signer API - Olivia: legal attestation wording + assessor check - Product: draft pricing for sales by EOW
kevin: I'll post the cost sheet by Friday.
ben: I'll prototype a verify script and a minimal manifest JSON example.
olivia: Will ping our assessor and flag contract clauses.
sarah: Thanks team. Keeping CX Bank informed that we can propose an archival evidence add-on.
